D_JOB01.document_text:
Job Description - Junior Data Analyst
Role Summary
The Junior Data Analyst supports routine data extraction, cleaning, reporting, dashboard preparation, and interpretation of business information for internal teams.
Key Responsibilities
Extract and combine data from structured business databases.
Clean, validate, and organize datasets before analysis.
Prepare recurring reports using Advanced Microsoft Excel.
Build and maintain Power BI dashboards for operational reporting.
Write SQL queries for data retrieval and summary analysis.
Communicate findings clearly to non-technical colleagues.
Maintain accurate documentation for reports and data processes.
Required Technical Skills
SQL
Advanced Microsoft Excel
Power BI or Tableau
Data cleaning and validation
Basic data visualization and reporting
Required Professional Skills
Analytical thinking
Attention to detail
Clear written and verbal communication
Ability to work collaboratively with a team
Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, or a related field.
One to two years of relevant analytical, reporting, internship, or junior-level experience is preferred.
Selection Note
This job description states the employer-side requirements for the role. It does not describe the skills, qualifications, or experience of any particular applicant.

D_COURSE01.document_text:
Course Brochure - Certificate in Practical Data Analytics
Course Overview
This introductory programme is designed to develop practical foundations in data preparation, querying, spreadsheet analysis, dashboard creation, and basic programming for analytics.
Modules
Advanced Excel: formulas, PivotTables, charts, and Power Query
SQL fundamentals: filtering, joins, grouping, and summary queries
Power BI: data import, basic modelling, visualizations, and dashboard design
Introduction to Python for data analysis
Data cleaning and validation principles
Communicating analytical findings with simple reports and presentations
Learning Outcomes
Prepare and clean small structured datasets.
Use Excel and SQL for routine analysis tasks.
Create a basic interactive Power BI dashboard.
Write introductory Python code for simple data manipulation.
Explain key findings from a small analysis task.
Entry Requirements
Basic computer literacy.
Ability to work with files, folders, and standard office applications.
No previous programming experience is required.
Completion
A certificate is issued only after successful completion of the required assessments and practical activities.
Not specified in this brochure: course fee, external accreditation status, or guaranteed employment/job placement.

D_EMP01.document_text:
Employability Skills Development Guide
This is an independent synthetic career-guidance document created for chatbot evaluation. It is not a government policy, official labour-market report, or accredited qualification framework.
Purpose
The guide outlines five general skill areas that can support career preparation and workplace readiness. The skills are presented as development areas for reflection and practice, not as a prediction of employment.
Communication
Express ideas clearly in writing and conversation, listen actively, and adapt messages to the audience.
Practice giving a one-minute explanation of a project or task.
Ask for feedback on clarity in written messages and presentations.
Digital Literacy
Use common digital tools responsibly and confidently for communication, information handling, and routine work tasks.
Practice with spreadsheets, document tools, shared drives, and online collaboration platforms.
Learn basic data privacy and account-security habits.
Analytical Thinking
Break problems into smaller parts, compare evidence, identify patterns, and justify conclusions.
Work through small case problems using available data.
Explain why a conclusion follows from the evidence used.
Teamwork
Contribute reliably to shared tasks, coordinate responsibilities, and communicate respectfully with others.
Take a defined role in a group project or volunteer activity.
Document agreed responsibilities and follow up on progress.
Continuous Learning
Identify knowledge gaps, seek appropriate learning resources, and reflect on progress over time.
Set one short monthly learning goal.
Keep a simple record of what was learned and how it was applied.
Using This Guide
A reader can select one or two development areas at a time, choose a practical activity, and review progress after several weeks. The guide does not state that every reader lacks these skills, and it does not guarantee an employment outcome.
